const RIGHT = 3;
const UPLEFT = 4;
const UPRIGHT = 5;
const DOWNLEFT = 6;

$dy = [1, -1, 0, 0, 1, 1, -1, -1];

$MAX = 5 * 30 + 5;

// marked[x][y][dir][lev][far]
$marked = [];

// mp: associative array for (x,y) -> bool

$t = [];

function rot($dir) {
    global $UP, $DOWN, $LEFT, $RIGHT, $UPLEFT, $UPRIGHT, $DOWNLEFT, $DOWNRIGHT;
    if ($dir == $UP) {
        return [$UPLEFT, $UPRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == $DOWN) {
        return [$DOWNLEFT, $DOWNRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == $LEFT) {
        return [$UPLEFT, $DOWNLEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == $RIGHT) {
        return [$UPRIGHT, $DOWNRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == $UPLEFT) {
        return [$UP, $LEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == $UPRIGHT) {
        return [$UP, $RIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == $DOWNLEFT) {
        return [$DOWN, $LEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == $DOWNRIGHT) {
        return [$DOWN, $RIGHT];
    }
    return [0, 0];
}

<?php
define("UP", 0);
define("DOWN", 1);
define("LEFT", 2);
define("RIGHT", 3);
define("UPLEFT", 4);
define("UPRIGHT", 5);
define("DOWNLEFT", 6);
define("DOWNRIGHT", 7);

$dx = [0, 0, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1];
$dy = [1, -1, 0, 0, 1, 1, -1, -1];

define("MAX", 5 * 30 + 5);

// marked[x][y][dir][lev][far]
$marked = [];
// Initialize marked as a nested array or use a hash map for sparse storage
// Given dimensions: 2*MAX x 2*MAX x 8 x 32 x 6
// Using a hash map (associative array) is more memory efficient for sparse data in PHP
// Key: "x,y,dir,lev,far" => true

$mp = []; // map<pair<int, int>, bool> -> key "x,y" => true
$t = [];

function rot($dir) {
    if ($dir == UP) {
        return [UPLEFT, UPRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == DOWN) {
        return [DOWNLEFT, DOWNRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == LEFT) {
        return [UPLEFT, DOWNLEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == RIGHT) {
        return [UPRIGHT, DOWNRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == UPLEFT) {
        return [UP, LEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == UPRIGHT) {
        return [UP, RIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == DOWNLEFT) {
        return [DOWN, LEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == DOWNRIGHT) {
        return [DOWN, RIGHT];
    }
    return [0, 0];
}

// Node representation as an array
// [x, y, dir, lev, far]

$n = (int)trim(fgets(STDIN));
for ($i = 1; $i <= $n; $i++) {
    $t[$i] = (int)trim(fgets(STDIN));
}

$ans = 0;

// Queue implementation using array
$Q = [];
$Q[] = [MAX, MAX, UP, 1, 1];

// Mark initial state
$key = "MAX,MAX,UP,1,1";
$marked[$key] = true;

$mpKey = "MAX,MAX";
$mp[$mpKey] = true;
$ans++;

while (!empty($Q)) {
    // Pop from front
    $v = array_shift($Q);
    $vx = $v[0];
    $vy = $v[1];
    $vdir = $v[2];
    $vlev = $v[3];
    $vfar = $v[4];

    $posKey = "$vx,$vy";
    if (!isset($mp[$posKey])) {
        $mp[$posKey] = true;
        $ans++;
    }

    $lev = $vlev;
    $far = $vfar;

    $x2 = $vx;
    $y2 = $vy;

    if ($lev == $n + 1) {
        continue;
    }

    if ($far != $t[$lev]) {
        $x2 += $dx[$vdir];
        $y2 += $dy[$vdir];
        
        // Check bounds? The original code assumes MAX is large enough.
        // Original: marked[x2][y2][v.dir][lev][far + 1]
        $newFar = $far + 1;
        $mKey = "$x2,$y2,$vdir,$lev,$newFar";
        if (isset($marked[$mKey])) {
            continue;
        }
        $marked[$mKey] = true;
        $Q[] = [$x2, $y2, $vdir, $lev, $newFar];
    } else {
        $dirs = rot($vdir);
        $dir1 = $dirs[0];
        $dir2 = $dirs[1];
        
        $newLev = $lev + 1;
        
        $mKey1 = "$vx,$vy,$dir1,$newLev,0";
        if (!isset($marked[$mKey1])) {
            $marked[$mKey1] = true;
            $Q[] = [$vx, $vy, $dir1, $newLev, 0];
        }
        
        $mKey2 = "$vx,$vy,$dir2,$newLev,0";
        if (!isset($marked[$mKey2])) {
            $marked[$mKey2] = true;
            $Q[] = [$vx, $vy, $dir2, $newLev, 0];
        }
    }
}

echo $ans . "\n";

<?php
const UP = 0;
const DOWN = 1;
const LEFT = 2;
const RIGHT = 3;
const UPLEFT = 4;
const UPRIGHT = 5;
const DOWNLEFT = 6;
const DOWNRIGHT = 7;

$dx = [0, 0, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1];
$dy = [1, -1, 0, 0, 1, 1, -1, -1];

const MAX = 5 * 30 + 5;

function rot($dir) {
    if ($dir == UP) {
        return [UPLEFT, UPRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == DOWN) {
        return [DOWNLEFT, DOWNRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == LEFT) {
        return [UPLEFT, DOWNLEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == RIGHT) {
        return [UPRIGHT, DOWNRIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == UPLEFT) {
        return [UP, LEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == UPRIGHT) {
        return [UP, RIGHT];
    }
    if ($dir == DOWNLEFT) {
        return [DOWN, LEFT];
    }
    if ($dir == DOWNRIGHT) {
        return [DOWN, RIGHT];
    }
    return [0, 0];
}

source_data.prob_desc_description: One tradition of welcoming the New Year is launching fireworks into the sky. Usually a launched firework flies vertically upward for some period of time, then explodes, splitting into several parts flying in different directions. Sometimes those parts also explode after some period of time, splitting into even more parts, and so on.Limak, who lives in an infinite grid, has a single firework. The behaviour of the firework is described with a recursion depth n and a duration for each level of recursion t1, t2, ..., tn. Once Limak launches the firework in some cell, the firework starts moving upward. After covering t1 cells (including the starting cell), it explodes and splits into two parts, each moving in the direction changed by 45 degrees (see the pictures below for clarification). So, one part moves in the top-left direction, while the other one moves in the top-right direction. Each part explodes again after covering t2 cells, splitting into two parts moving in directions again changed by 45 degrees. The process continues till the n-th level of recursion, when all 2n - 1 existing parts explode and disappear without creating new parts. After a few levels of recursion, it's possible that some parts will be at the same place and at the same time — it is allowed and such parts do not crash.Before launching the firework, Limak must make sure that nobody stands in cells which will be visited at least once by the firework. Can you count the number of those cells?
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print one integer, denoting the number of cells which will be visited at least once by any part of the firework.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 30) — the total depth of the recursion. The second line contains n integers t1, t2, ..., tn (1 ≤ ti ≤ 5). On the i-th level each of 2i - 1 parts will cover ti cells before exploding.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteFor the first sample, the drawings below show the situation after each level of recursion. Limak launched the firework from the bottom-most red cell. It covered t1 = 4 cells (marked red), exploded and divided into two parts (their further movement is marked green). All explosions are marked with an 'X' character. On the last drawing, there are 4 red, 4 green, 8 orange and 23 pink cells. So, the total number of visited cells is 4 + 4 + 8 + 23 = 39.
